Theme

School & learning

slow adjective

slow to learn

also slow to learn, slow on the uptake, dim

classical

Ter. Heaut. 4.5.28: Prōrsum nihil intellegō. — Hui, tardus es. (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Ac. 1.31: sēnsūs hebetēs et tardī (Lewis & Short)

tardus, tarda, tardum

declension

slow of understanding, dull

Other words

  • sēgnis, sēgnis, sēgne — sluggish, slack

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 31, for “slow to learn”

    Lewis & Short: slow and inactive, lazy; it says unwillingness more than difficulty.

See also clever, lazy.

SourcesLewis & Short: tardus · Lewis & Short: segnis

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 31.
